CHAPTER 6 — COMPLETE DRIVER, PIT STOPS, STRATEGY AND SPLINES

Final main chapter: a reproducible complete race, not an isolated pit helper.
The checkpoint includes every helper source it needs in its own directory.

Main sequence
1. One deliberately requested stop before automatic strategy.
2. Assigned pit, occupancy, entry/start/end/exit, capture region and no-pit case.
3. Seven-knot distance/offset route, signed side and unwrapped lap coordinates.
4. Entry braking, pit speed cap, stopping and capture, service callback.
5. Exit route, waiting for merge space, traffic/recovery ownership and resets.
6. Lap fuel accounting, actual refuelling, remaining distance, tank and repair limits.
7. Integrated update cycle and a longer race with repeated service visits.

Spline companion — retain the complete mathematical route
- Values and slopes at both endpoints determine a cubic.
- Normalize each interval; chain-rule factor h for derivatives.
- Solve all four coefficients, present the four Hermite basis functions.
- Map to nested/Horner evaluation and binary interval search.
- C1 versus C2 continuity, signed slopes, zero-slope transitions, overshoot.
- Duplicate knots, finite input, endpoint policy and out-of-domain evaluation.
- Offset graph versus world path; target point and actual body trajectory.
- Worked numerical example, plots and endpoint/derivative checks.

Current engine audit
- Side pits may be shared; pitCarIndex controls occupancy. Separate-path pits
  are not assigned by the current race initializer.
- Service requires RM_CMD_PIT_ASKED, a free assigned pit, longitudinal capture
  bounds, lateral placement and both body-frame speeds below 1 m/s.
- The engine clears the request during service. A cleared request does not mean
  the car has left the pit lane.
- Capture bounds and current pit metadata must be used, not driver-index formulas.
- Fuel and repair requests are normalized by the engine; tire-change support
  exists and must not be described as universally absent.
- Pit road-side travel intentionally leaves the main-road corridor: ordinary
  edge feedback and overtaking must not overwrite the pit route.

Verification
- Hermite endpoint values/slopes, independent basis comparison, duplicate and
  boundary cases; route ordering and start-line wrap.
- Solo service, fuel/damage strategy, repeated stops with corrected fuel accounting.
- Entry and exit rules, stopping capture, pit occupancy, absent/unsupported pits.
- Traffic-aware rejoining and ordinary opponents; recovery inhibited in service.
- Build and run the complete checkpoint with no earlier source folders present.
